Public Lands Day to be observed at Coonskin Park
CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WV News) — National Public Lands Day will be observed Saturday, Sept. 27, at Coonskin Park.
The day's events will take place at Shelter 20 in the upper park. The schedule events includes 9 a.m. coffee and donuts and volunteer trail work at 9:30 a.m.
At noon, a free lunch will be served, followed by hiking, biking and running from 1-4 p.m. Attendees are encouraged to bring shoes and mountain bikes.
At 1:30 p.m., there will be a guided hike on Alice Knight Trail to the Coonskin Grotto.
New and improved trail maps will be available and Coonskin experts will be on hand to answer questions. For more information, visit CoonskinTrailsCoalition.com.
Little Kanawha Reading Series at Glenville State to host first event of semester
GLENVILLE, W.Va. (WV News) — The Little Kanawha Reading Series at Glenville State University will host its first reading of the fall semester Sept. 25 at 4 p.m. at the Robert F. Kidd Library.
The event will feature poet, educator and instructional technologist Traci Probst. The reading is free and open to the public.
Probst’s work bridges the worlds of creative writing and higher education. A Glenville State University alumna and English Education major, she was named Glenville State College Student of the Year in 1990.
She currently serves as an instructional technologist and adjunct professor at West Virginia Wesleyan College, and is president of the Arts Council of Weston.
Her poetry has been published in Bouillabaisse (1994), Wordwrights (1998), Appalachian Heritage (2000), and Vandalia (2016).
The Little Kanawha Reading Series provides a showcase for a diversity of literary forms and voices in order to acknowledge and enrich the cultural heritage of Appalachia and the communities around the Little Kanawha River.
Readings are also streamed on the university’s YouTube channel.
Third annual Breath of Life Recovery Walk set for Sept. 13
RIPLEY, W.Va. (WV News) — The third annual Breath of Life Recovery Walk will take place on the Jackson County Courthouse lawn from 12-3 p.m. on Saturday, Sept. 13.
Some of the groups that will be represented include Hope House Ministries, Hope for All, Recovery Point, and Jackson County QRT.
Pastor Jay Johnson of The Cross Church in Ripley will deliver the message, and there will also be words from Dee Rhodes, the home confinement officer for the county.
Three speakers will share their journeys from addiction to recovery.
Everyone is urged to bring a pair of new or gently used shoes in memory of someone lost to addiction. Two gift cards will be given away, and there will also be free food.
The final event will be the walk at 3 p.m. As everyone joins together and walks around the courthouse square, there will be celebration and remembrance.
For information on Breath of Life Recovery, follow the group on Facebook.
Organizers offer tips ahead of Mothman Festival in Point Pleasant
POINT PLEASANT, W.Va. (WV News) — Organizers of the annual Mothman Festival are sharing tips to help visitors make the most of their trip to downtown Point Pleasant on Sept. 20-21.
Because the city experiences a surge in visitors and limited internet access during the event, attendees are encouraged to bring cash to avoid long lines at the ATM. Comfortable walking shoes, sunscreen and water are also recommended, as festivalgoers should expect to be on their feet throughout the day.
Parking is available along both the upper and lower parts of Main Street, with some local businesses offering paid options. The city also will provide overflow parking at Krodel Park for a fee, with limited shuttle service from the county. Organizers advise that walking is often faster than waiting for the shuttle, and they stress that the earlier visitors arrive, the better their chances of finding convenient parking.
Officials ask attendees to leave their dogs at home, citing concerns over large crowds, high temperatures and the risk of pets being stepped on. Those hoping to participate in the popular TNT Hayride are reminded that tickets are sold on a first-come, first-served basis beginning at 10 a.m. at the information tent beside the post office. Sales are cash only, and exact change is appreciated. Tickets traditionally sell out quickly, with no advance sales available.
The festival’s busiest time is Saturday, though organizers note that those seeking a more relaxed experience may prefer Sunday. Some visitors arrive as early as Thursday or Friday to browse local Main Street shops, visit the Mothman Museum, and take photos with the Mothman statue before crowds gather.
Organizers also caution drivers not to park in handicap-designated spaces unless they display the proper placard. These spaces, which are marked on the festival map, fill quickly and are strictly enforced.
